source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 11: a x b = 0 and a . b = 0 together force a = 0 or b = 0 (book p.283). Answer key PDF 312 agrees.

blocks.prompt: 11. If \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \underline{0}\) and \(\underline{a} \cdot \underline{b} = 0\), what conclusion can be drawn about \(\underline{a}\) or \(\underline{b}\)?
blocks.explanation:
Yeh soch-samajh (reasoning) ka sawal hai, hisaab kam hai.
Dekhna hai ke dono shartein (conditions) ek saath kya batati hain.
Plan: har shart ko \(\sin\theta\) ya \(\cos\theta\) ki baat mein badlein; dono ek saath zero nahi ho sakte.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \underline{0}\) aur \(\underline{a} \cdot \underline{b} = 0\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\underline{a}\) ya \(\underline{b}\) ke baare mein kya natija nikalta hai.
Tareeqa: \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\) aur \(\underline{a} \cdot \underline{b} = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\cos\theta\). Cross product zero ka matlab parallel, dot product zero ka matlab perpendicular. Kya koi do vectors ek saath parallel bhi aur perpendicular bhi ho sakte hain? Yahi sochna hai.

Maan lein dono vectors non-zero hain
\[|\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \sin\theta = 0\]
\[|\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\cos\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \cos\theta = 0\]
Kyun: Agar dono ki lambai zero nahi to \(|\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\) se divide kar sakte hain. Pehli baat kehti hai vectors parallel hain (angle 0 ya 180 degree), doosri kehti hai perpendicular (angle 90 degree).

Yeh namumkin hai
\[\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\]
\[0 + 0 \ne 1\]
Kyun: Koi bhi angle aisa nahi jis ka sine aur cosine dono zero hon. Ek hi waqt mein 0 degree aur 90 degree ka angle nahi ho sakta. Is liye hamara maanna (ke dono non-zero hain) ghalat tha.

Yahi baat ek line mein
\[|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|^2 + (\underline{a} \cdot \underline{b})^2 = |\underline{a}|^2|\underline{b}|^2\]
\[0 + 0 = |\underline{a}|^2|\underline{b}|^2\]
Kyun: Dono ke squares jama kiye aur \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\) lagaya. Is liye \(|\underline{a}||\underline{b}| = 0\), yani \(|\underline{a}| = 0\) ya \(|\underline{b}| = 0\). Yeh tareeqa zyada saaf hai kyunke is mein angle ki zaroorat hi nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\underline{a} = \underline{0}:\ \underline{0} \times \underline{b} = \underline{0},\ \underline{0} \cdot \underline{b} = 0\]
Kyun: Zero vector waqai dono shartein poori karta hai; kitab ka Note bhi yahi kehta hai ke zero vector har vector ke parallel bhi hai aur perpendicular bhi. Is liye yahi ek mumkin natija hai.
blocks.final_answer: Kam az kam ek vector, \(\underline{a}\) ya \(\underline{b}\), zero vector hai.
